title: Cost Model API observability + alerts (latency, errors, cache hit, estimate-vs-metered drift)
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Context
- Console cost breakdown and Optimize what-if flows are becoming dependent on cost-model-service. We need production-grade dashboards + alerting before staged rollout expands beyond canary tenants.
- This ticket covers: service SLI dashboards, alert rules, and a drift/mismatch detector comparing SCM estimate outputs vs metered attribution (where available).

Goals
1) Dashboards
- Cost Model API: request volume, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, saturation, per-region breakdown.
- Cache behavior: internal memoization/shared cache hit ratio (where enabled), cache latency impact, eviction rates.
- Input validation: rejected requests by reason (missing required dims, unsupported version, invalid units) with top callers.
- Version mix: requested vs negotiated versions over time.
- Mismatch/drift: compare estimated cost breakdown vs metered attribution on a fixed canary prompt set; show absolute and percent deltas + component-level deltas.

2) Alerts (actionable, low-noise)
- Availability/error-rate: alert on sustained elevated 5xx and/or increased client-visible failures.
- Latency: alert on p95 and p99 thresholds; separate warnings from paging.
- Dependency criticality: Console pages degrade if SCM is slow; alert on timeouts and upstream dependency failures (telemetry lookup, catalog lookup) separately.
- Drift detector: page only on large sustained drift beyond agreed thresholds; otherwise ticket-only.

Non-goals
- Changing client timeouts/retry policies (tracked elsewhere).
- Billing reconciliation tooling (SCM is not invoice source-of-truth).

Implementation notes
- Metrics source: cost-model-service Prometheus (HTTP server + internal stages).
- Prefer RED metrics per endpoint: rate/errors/duration; include endpoint name (estimate/explain), negotiated_version, region, deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private) with strict cardinality controls.
- Cache hit ratio: define explicitly as hits/(hits+misses) at the service layer; expose separate counters for memoization vs shared cache if both exist.
- Drift detector: join on request_id for canary harness OR compute deltas inside canary job and export as time series; do NOT attempt high-cardinality per-tenant mismatch metrics.
- All dashboards to live in the standard Observability Pack with JSON templates; alerts in the standard rules repo used by SRE.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Grafana dashboard: "SCM / Cost Model API Overview" with RED metrics, per-region facets, and endpoint panels.
- [x] Grafana dashboard: "SCM / Cost Model API Internals" with stage breakdown (validation, catalog lookup, telemetry lookup, compute, response serialization), cache hit ratio, and saturation signals.
- [x] Grafana dashboard: "SCM / Drift & Mismatch" showing estimate-vs-metered deltas on canary prompt set (overall + component breakdown) + links to runbook.
- [x] Alert rules implemented with clear paging vs ticket routing:
  - paging: sustained high 5xx / availability breach, p99 latency breach impacting Console dependency
  - ticket: elevated 4xx due to validation (likely client regression), drift warnings, cache hit ratio degradation
- [x] Runbook link embedded in alerts and dashboard annotations: how to triage (check version negotiation changes, upstream dependency error spikes, cache hit drop, telemetry delay).
- [x] Cardinality review completed with Logan/Nadia/Thomas: ensure new labels don’t explode series count.

Owners / reviewers
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (review), Rafael Mendes (implementation)
- Platform: Priya Natarajan (sign-off), Ethan Park (service metrics)
- Observability standards: Allison Grant (dashboard conventions)
- Telemetry: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (dimension + cardinality review)

Rollout plan
- Land dashboards + alerts disabled-by-default.
- Enable alerts in staging for 48h to tune thresholds.
- Enable warning alerts in prod during canary (5% tenants), then enable paging alerts after 1 week of stable signal.

Open questions
- Drift thresholds: propose page if >10% delta sustained for 30m OR >$X absolute delta per 1k requests (needs PM alignment).
comments: 2025-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Started with existing service metrics; added stage timers around validation/catalog/telemetry/compute. Noticed current hist buckets were too coarse for sub-100ms segments; will adjust to match p95/p99 reporting needs.

2025-02-13 (Allison Grant): Please follow dashboard naming/templating conventions (standard variables: region, deployment_mode, endpoint). Avoid per-model panels; model_id should not be a dashboard variable due to cardinality.

2025-02-18 (Logan Wright): Cardinality check: negotiated_version is OK (small set). Do NOT tag alerts with tenant_id or route_id. For drift, keep it canary-only; export aggregated series from the canary job instead of emitting per-request comparisons.

2025-02-24 (Sean Gallagher): Align alert thresholds with draft SLOs: warning at p95>250ms (5m), page at p99>600ms (10m) for estimate endpoint. For error rate, page at 5xx>1% (10m) when RPS>baseline; ticket at 5xx>0.3% (30m). Add separate panel for upstream dependency failures (catalog/telemetry) to prevent noisy paging.

2025-03-03 (Rafael Mendes): Drift dashboard wired to perf-canary job output. We see occasional spikes during telemetry backfill; added annotation to exclude "telemetry_delay" windows and exported a separate time series to make this explicit.
2025-03-11 (Priya Natarajan): Signed off. Dashboards look good; alerts enabled in staging and prod warnings only. Paging alerts scheduled to enable after 7 days if no false positives.
